prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale:ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery;predictable latency,documented quality,retained external interfaces. Elements:Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice)—safety,commands,passes,anomalies,routing,handover;Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs)—navigation,maneuvers,orbit predictions,visibility/pointing→planning;Mission Planning System(Cedar)—authoritative candidate observation/contact timelines,contact booking requests(service,antenna,elevation,volume,priority),operational constraints→plans;Command Validation Gateway—mandatory pre-uplink checks;Network Control System(Lantern)—authoritative circuits,routing,allocations,readiness,contact records;antenna status,link configuration,timing references,routing readiness→Bluebell;Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters)—assignments,availability,conflicts,maintenance,staffing,site coordination;Antenna Deicing Notice,mandatory maintenance-critical pre-acquisition tasks;Orbit Determination Engine—tracking→orbit/state,visibility,maneuver/pointing basis,qualified-pass Doppler Residual Report;Telemetry Ingest Service—frames/contact/flow indicators→operations,engineering,processing;validates framing/time continuity,records metadata,distinguishes gaps/interruptions;post-contact Pass Replay Packet;Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse/console discussions/shift logs)—processing,calibration,distribution;Primary Processing Cluster(nominal),Backup Processing Cluster(controlled failover);Product Quality Service—pre-distribution checks;Long Term Archive—authoritative data/products/evidence;User Services Portal—search,orders,status,support,observation requests,accepted/pending-review states. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate)—commands/low-rate telemetry→Bluebell. Actors:Spacecraft Operations Team—safety/authorization,mode/power/thermal/attitude/counters/storage/fault-protection monitoring,late-request review;console lead—pass declaration,Gateway command authorization,unexpected-configuration pause;telemetry engineer—quality/loss/latency/continuity/command-confidence;spacecraft systems engineer—health/flight rules/anomaly context;Flight Dynamics Team—validated contact tracking/timestamps→Mistral,separates clock bias/tracking error;Payload Calibration Team—quality,approved Calibration Patch Bundle→Forgehouse;Cybersecurity Desk—monitoring/escalation,Security Exception Ticket;local station

New part:
S108: The draft schedule covers payload imaging, recorder management, housekeeping activities, and expected support from the North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna.
S109: For high-volume acquisitions, the schedule also accounts for downlink opportunities through the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna.
S110: The Payload Processing Facility receives planning metadata needed to prepare downstream processing expectations without treating the planning schedule as a commitment to deliver products.
S111: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are considered during planning only to verify that expected acquisition loads remain compatible with routine processing capacity.
S112: Juniper confirms that planned station use is compatible with network maintenance windows before the schedule is released for command preparation.
S113: The Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Antenna Deicing Notice to assess whether planned support can proceed without adding contingency contact margin.
S114: The Mission Planning System flags conflicts when two activities compete for the same spacecraft resource, ground station resource, or operational staffing interval.
S115: Constraint checking includes slew time, sun-angle limits, power balance, thermal recovery time, recorder capacity, command load size, and required separation between incompatible activities.
S116: The Flight Dynamics Team reviews cases where orbital uncertainty or contact geometry could reduce the execution margin for a planned acquisition or downlink.
S117: The Payload Calibration Team reviews planned calibration activities when they share resources with revenue observations or affect instrument configuration states.
S118: After schedule convergence, the Mission Planning System exports a command preparation package to the command engineering workflow at the Mission Control Center.
S119: The Command Validation Gateway, also called Osprey in this section, performs independent validation of command stacks before they are eligible for operational approval.
S120: Command stack validation checks syntax, timing, parameter ranges, sequencing rules, spacecraft mode compatibility, and consistency with the approved schedule baseline.
S121: The Command Validation Gateway rejects command stacks that contain unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired configuration references, or activities outside the planning authority window.
S122: The Telemetry Ingest Service is consulted for the latest spacecraft state needed to confirm that the command assumptions still match actual configuration and health.
S123: The Orbit Determination Engine provides the current orbital solution used to confirm time-tagged events, contact visibility, and any attitude-dependent observation geometry.
S124: The Product Quality Service may add planning feedback when previous acquisitions indicate that a requested geometry or instrument mode is unlikely to meet quality objectives.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
